text:
lena: quick heads-up 12 linkcheck caught a weird class of failures after the docusaurus move: duplicate/missing anchors coming from headings that contain inline code or parentheses.
omar: paste the CI lines?
lena:
```
[linkcheck] WARNING: ./guides/upgrade.mdx: anchor not found: feature-v2
[linkcheck] WARNING: ./reference/cli.mdx: duplicate anchor: feature-v2 (from 'Feature (v2)' and 'Feature `v2`')
```
rui: ahh, we have two heading variants: `# Feature (v2)` and `# Feature `v2``. mkdocs slugifier used to drop parens and backticks differently; docusaurus normalizes inline code by removing backticks but keeps parens sometimes. result = either the same slug (collision) or missing anchor depending on page order.
lena: repro'd locally: both create `feature-v2` slug in docusaurus but mkdocs had `feature-v2` and `feature-v2-1` previously (so cross-links broke).
omar: what's the mitigation? change authors' headings? big lift.
rui: two small, safe steps we can take: 1) heading-only sanitizer in docs CI that removes backticks, strips surrounding parens for short parenthetical suffixes like `(v2)` or `(beta)`, and collapses punctuation runs. 2) run a slug-collision detector during the docs-lint step that auto-generates a frontmatter alias when collisions are detected (only for the pair(s) that collide) so existing links keep working. fallback is to create a one-off maintenance backfill.
lena: can you sketch the sanitizer? keep it conservative and only touch headings.
rui: sure, perl one-liner for CI pre-linkcheck (heading-only):
```bash
# run in docs-ci before linkcheck
for f in $(git ls-files '*.md' '*.mdx'); do
  perl -C -0777 -pe \
    "s/(?m)^\s*#\s*(.*)/'# '.(my $h=$1)=~s/`([^`]*)`/$1/gr =~ s/\s*\((v\d+|beta|alpha)\)\s*$//igr =~ s/[^\\S\\n]{2,}/ /gr/ger" -i "\$f"
done
```
(note: this only removes backticks from inline code in headings and strips short parenthetical suffixes like `(v2)` — intentional narrow scope)
omar: OK. and the alias generator?
rui: small node script in docs-lint: slugify all headings (using docusaurus slugify) and detect duplicates across a file. if duplicate slugs found and no explicit frontmatter alias present, add a minimal frontmatter block with `slug_aliases: ["original-heading-slug"]` to the later file to preserve incoming links. we only auto-add when collision is detected to avoid touching most files.
lena: that seems reasonable. please add unit tests: a test vector with `Feature (v2)`, `Feature 0code` and `Feature v2` to ensure sanitizer + aliaser behave as expected.
ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1600 by rui — adds heading sanitizer, slug-collision detector, test vector, and a short note in docs/migration.md explaining the policy. CI queued.
lena: pinging @omar for a quick review; aim for fast-track (`docs:quick`) since it's low-risk and fixes live linkcheck failures.
ci-bot: CI started for PR #1600 (linkcheck, docs-lint, unit tests).
ci-bot: CI passed for PR #1600.
infra-bot: running non-destructive backfill dry-run to see how many files would be touched.
infra-bot: dry-run backfill: 13 files would be modified; 3 files would receive auto-generated frontmatter alias blocks; 10 files sanitized (heading-only changes).
lena: prefer one infra maintenance commit (signed bot) instead of many tiny PRs. can infra apply?
infra-bot: applying maintenance commit now. commit message: "docs: sanitize heading inline code and add slug aliases for collisions (backfill)" pushed by infra-bot.
infra-bot: backfill complete: 13 files modified, 3 frontmatter alias entries added. linkcheck re-run on main: no fragment warnings.
omar: confirmed preview build shows anchors stable and existing links resolving. good call adding the alias fallback.
rui: i'll add a short paragraph to the contributor guide advising to avoid inline code in headings and to prefer plain suffixes like `v2` without parentheses. also left the sanitizer intentionally narrow so we don't rewrite content broadly.
lena: thanks all 44d. closing thread once contributor-guide PR merges. :white_check_mark:
